requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap added on node1
requirements.summary: zram-generator configured with zram-size=1024 (MiB), compression-algorithm=zstd; swapon/zramctl confirm /dev/zram0 at 1G/1024M with zstd compression active, exceeding the 512MB minimum. Functional memory-pressure test showed real compression (37.4M data compressed to 5.5M).

requirements.requirement: Compressed swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: zram0 configured with swap-priority=100 vs existing /dev/vda2 disk swap at priority -2. Post-config and post-reboot swapon/proc-swaps output both confirm zram0 ranks above disk swap, and the memory-pressure test showed zram0 absorbing swapped pages while disk swap stayed nearly idle.

requirements.requirement: Compressed swap active at boot (persists across restart, no manual steps)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart state captured (boot_id bf4e9cbb...), a real reboot was performed and acknowledged (systemd-run scheduled reboot, node went unreachable, then returned with a new boot_id 86c84e66...). Post-restart verification shows /dev/zram0 (1024M, zstd, priority 100) and dev-zram0.swap / systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service both active automatically with no manual intervention, disk swap still present at lower priority.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — at least 512MB compressed in-memory swap, priority over disk-backed swap, and activation at boot — are directly and coherently satisfied. The executor installed zram-generator, configured a 1GiB zstd-compressed zram0 device at swap-priority 100 (versus disk swap's -2), proved compression and priority preference under real memory pressure, and then performed an actual node reboot with boot-identity verification before and after, confirming the zram swap activates automatically at boot with no manual steps. The only notable issue is a bounded, ultimately non-damaging troubleshooting detour where the executor stopped and tried to manually reset the already-working zram device during debugging, which failed twice before the device was found correctly configured again.
limitations: It is not fully clear from the captured trace whether the zram device's recovery after the failed manual reset attempts (cmd-4430de4a6db041c4, cmd-a9282d9f7ebd435f) was due to an explicit corrective action not captured or automatic systemd re-activation; this is inferred rather than directly observed.

The task instruction does not itself require restart/persistence testing as a contract term separate from 'active at boot', but the executor's node-restart evidence protocol independently and adequately covers this via the observed boot-identity change and post-restart service verification.

operational_hygiene.summary: Core implementation (install zram-generator, write config, start unit) was clean and minimal. However, during debugging of config precedence, the executor performed an unnecessary troubleshooting sequence that mutated an already-correctly-configured swap device: it stopped systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service and reset the zram device (cmd-683150b4073d4d41), then made two failed manual attempts to recreate it including swapoff/zramctl -r/rmmod/modprobe (cmd-4430de4a6db041c4, cmd-a9282d9f7ebd435f), both returning 'device busy' errors. This was not needed since the config was already verified working immediately after cmd-915234b2fc8740aa. The device was subsequently found correctly configured again (cmd-654317c9b135496c, cmd-2e70317388dd4338) without an explicit corrective command in the trace, so it is unclear whether this self-resolved via systemd re-activation or the intervening reads simply observed a device that had recovered on its own; final state and the later reboot both confirm no lasting damage. No other residue, abandoned files, failed services, or exposure issues were observed; after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed services and only expected boot-scoped tmp/socket churn from the reboot.
